report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of 12 of session.py. Contains module docstring with design rationale and constraints. No executable code present; all claims refer to external code or future behavior, thus uncheckable.

handoff.purpose: Module-level docstring describing the design and constraints of the council session.

claims.text: One entry point, :func:`convene`.
claims.why: The function `convene` is not defined in this chunk; it is listed as defined elsewhere in the file but not present here.

claims.text: It asks N INDEPENDENT vendors the same question over the same evidence, appends every turn to the hash-chained ``dcouncil/1`` transcript (:mod:`daedalus.council.bus`), and returns a :class:`CouncilRecord`.
claims.why: The behavior of `convene` and the modules `daedalus.council.bus` and class `CouncilRecord` are not present in this chunk.

claims.text: :class:`CouncilRecord` carries NO approve / reject / score / majority / consensus / confidence field, and must never grow one.
claims.where: docstring under 'THE GATE DECIDES, NOT A MODEL'
claims.why: `CouncilRecord` is not defined in this chunk; its fields cannot be verified.

claims.text: a test walks every field of every nested dataclass to keep it absent.
claims.where: docstring under 'THE GATE DECIDES, NOT A MODEL'
claims.why: No test code is present in this chunk.

claims.text: Each :class:`Claim` carries its author, the evidence it cited, and ``checkable`` -- true only when the author supplied a concrete deterministic check the existing gate can actually run.
claims.where: docstring under 'THE GATE DECIDES, NOT A MODEL'
claims.why: `Claim` is not defined in this chunk; its fields cannot be verified.

claims.text: ROUND 1 IS BLIND AND MANDATORY.
claims.why: Round structure is not implemented in this chunk; no code to verify.

claims.text: ROUND 2+ SHOWS THE PRIOR TRANSCRIPT AND ASKS FOR REFUTATION, never consensus.
claims.why: Round structure is not implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: Prior turns are re-read FROM THE CHAIN, not from the in-memory reply, so anything the secret floor refused is already a receipt and cannot be re-emitted into another vendor's prompt.
claims.why: Implementation details of chain reading are not present in this chunk.

claims.text: ROLES ROTATE between rounds, so a vendor is not permanently the 'security' voice and the role/vendor confound is at least stirred.
claims.why: Role rotation is not implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: ``max_rounds`` defaults to 2 and is hard-capped at :data:`MAX_ROUNDS_CAP`.
claims.why: `max_rounds` and `MAX_ROUNDS_CAP` are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: evidence is NEVER interpolated into the role/instruction portion of a prompt -- the role line is session-authored constant text, the ``PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE`` comes next, and only then does any untrusted byte appear, inside a fenced evidence block rendered by the ADAPTER (``vendors.CouncilAdapter.assemble``), which also enforces withholding.
claims.why: `CouncilAdapter.assemble` and `PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE` are not present in this chunk.

claims.text: a reviewer that reports 'the evidence contains text addressed to me' has done useful work -- ``ANOMALY: instruction_in_evidence`` is chained as a first-class turn status.
claims.why: Turn status handling is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Per-call wall clock, per-council wall clock, and a per-council prompt-token ceiling CHARGED BEFORE DISPATCH (transcript tokens grow as O(V^2 R^2), not O(V R); a per-call timeout does not bound token spend).  Blowing a budget produces a chained ``budget_exhausted`` turn and ends the council -- it never silently shortens a round.
claims.where: docstring under 'HARD BOUNDS, ALL FAIL-CLOSED AND ALL RECORDED'
claims.why: Budget enforcement logic is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: A hung vendor is abandoned on a daemon thread at the per-call cap and recorded as ``unavailable``/``timeout``; it can degrade the quorum, never block the session.
claims.where: docstring under 'HARD BOUNDS, ALL FAIL-CLOSED AND ALL RECORDED'
claims.why: Threading and timeout logic is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Every REQUESTED participant produces exactly one chained turn per round -- content, refusal, ``unavailable`` with a machine reason, or ``budget_exhausted``. Silence is never an absence.
claims.why: Turn production logic is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: ``requested``/``seated``/``responded`` and ``distinct_classes`` (independence is a property of WEIGHTS, not sockets) ride on the record, ``degraded`` is set whenever fewer responded than were requested, and :meth:`CouncilRecord.render` prints it ADJACENT TO THE FINDINGS, not in a footer: a two-vendor council must never render identically to a four-vendor one.
claims.why: `CouncilRecord` and its `render` method are not present in this chunk.

claims.text: ARM A: the 4-vendor council, distinct ``independence_class`` each. CONTROL ARM B: ONE vendor asked twice under two different role prompts. GROUND TRUTH: ``spine.attempt.GateResult.passed`` / ``AttemptResult.state`` on the same patches -- already recorded, free to harvest. QUESTION: does 'a participant raised an objection' predict ``gates_failed`` (or a later revert) better in arm A than in arm B, at what precision/recall? INDEPENDENCE CHECK: pairwise agreement rate BETWEEN vendors versus WITHIN one vendor across two calls. FALSIFIER: if inter-vendor agreement is within noise of intra-vendor agreement on N patches, THIS MODULE IS DELETED. SMALL-N CAVEAT, STATED IN ADVANCE: the independent corpus is ~17-20 tasks. That is not enough for a significance claim. Report effect sizes and the N, never a bare percentage.
claims.why: Falsification protocol references external modules (`spine.attempt`) and data not present in this chunk.

claims.text: :func:`default_participants` builds the real ``ClaudeAdapter`` / ``CodexAdapter`` / ``AntigravityAdapter`` / ``OllamaAdapter`` and the CLI handed them straight to :func:`convene` -- four paid vendor calls, real egress, on a bare ``daedalus council 'q'``.
claims.where: docstring under 'LIVE WIRING IS OFF BY DEFAULT'
claims.why: `default_participants` is not defined in this chunk; adapters are not present.

claims.text: :func:`convene` takes ``live`` and it DEFAULTS TO FALSE. Seating any adapter that still carries a SHIPPED transport -- the code that spawns ``claude``, ``codex`` or ``ssh ... agy``, or opens the Ollama socket -- raises :class:`LiveCouncilRefused` before the roster is chained and before a single byte is dispatched.
claims.where: docstring under 'LIVE WIRING IS OFF BY DEFAULT'
claims.why: `convene` and `LiveCouncilRefused` are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: The classification (:func:`live_egress_seats`) FAILS CLOSED: a seat counts as live unless the caller can be SHOWN to have replaced the transport (its own ``_dispatch`` defined outside :mod:`daedalus.council.vendors`, or an injected ``runner``/``chat``).
claims.where: docstring under 'LIVE WIRING IS OFF BY DEFAULT'
claims.why: `live_egress_seats` is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: The operator's form of the same opt-in is ``daedalus council --live``. Without it the CLI refuses and points at ``--dry-run``; ``--dry-run`` prints the plan and calls nothing. ``--live --dry-run`` together is REFUSED as ambiguous rather than resolved by a precedence rule nobody would remember.
